title: Clone Graph
description:
Given a reference of a node in a **connected** undirected graph, return a **deep copy** (clone) of the graph.

Each node in the graph contains a value (`int val`) and a list (`List<Node> neighbors`) of its adjacent nodes. Every node's value equals its 1-based index (`1` to `n`).

Every node in the returned graph must be a brand-new `Node` instance — none of the nodes or neighbor references may point to any node in the original graph, and the original graph must not be modified. If the input node is `null`, return `null`.

In the test format, a graph is represented as a 1-indexed adjacency list `adjList`, where `adjList[i - 1]` lists the neighbors of node `i`, and the starting node passed to `cloneGraph` is node `1` (or `null` when `adjList` is empty).
constraints: The number of nodes in the graph is in the range [0, 100].
Node.val is unique for each node.
There are no repeated edges and no self-loops in the graph.
The graph is connected and all nodes can be visited starting from the given node.
hints: A graph can contain cycles, so naively recursing on neighbors without tracking visited nodes will cause infinite recursion.
Maintain a hash map mapping each original `Node` reference to its newly created cloned `Node`.
Create and store the clone in the map *before* recursively cloning (or enqueuing) its neighbors, so back-edges and cycles immediately link to the existing clone.

examples.explanation: All 4 nodes and all 4 undirected edges of the cycle (1-2-3-4-1) are deep-copied into fresh Node instances.
A single node with value 1 and no neighbors is cloned into a new Node(1, []).
The graph is empty (null input), so cloneGraph returns null.

inputs.name: adjList
inputs.description: 1-indexed adjacency list representing a connected undirected graph
